Check that you have enough fuel for the day
Make sure you have your passport in the car
Ensure you have a spare set of tyres in the boot

In a designated 'Taxi Rank' outside a train station
A legal parking space or a designated pick-up/drop-off point
Directly on a pedestrian crossing to save the passenger walking

To allow you to drive in bus lanes legally

Defacing, altering, or tampering with any details on the badge
Cleaning the badge with a damp cloth
Wearing the badge on a clip instead of a neck cord

A PHV badge does not exempt you from following normal road traffic signs and orders

bank.question: It is the driver's responsibility to ensure the vehicle is in a roadworthy condition before starting their shift

bank.question: What is the correct way to display your driver's identification badge while working?

Placing it on the dashboard facing outwards

To serve as a secondary form of ID for opening a bank account

Any driver with a standard UK driving licence

Only a driver who holds a valid Private Hire Driver's licence

bank.question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Fit and Proper' person test for drivers?

Ensuring the car is cleaned once a week
Taking the shortest possible route regardless of traffic
The safety and well-being of the passenger throughout the journey

options: Yes, as it takes longer to load the wheelchair
No, it is illegal to charge extra for carrying a wheelchair
Yes, but only if the wheelchair is electric
Only if the operator's price list explicitly allows it

bank.question: You only need to report a speeding fine to the council if it results in a driving disqualification
bank.explanation: All convictions, including driving offences and fixed penalty notices, must be reported to the licensing authority, usually within 7 days

bank.question: A person approaches you in the street and asks to be taken to a nearby train station. What is the correct way to handle this?
bank.explanation: While you can suggest they contact the operator, you must not accept the booking directly as 'plying for hire' is illegal for private hire drivers
options: Accept the booking if you have no current job assigned
Tell them to get into the car and you will start the meter
Explain that you can only take pre-booked journeys and they must contact the operator
Take the booking but ask the passenger to pay in cash only

bank.question: What is the legal consequence if you continue to drive for hire after your PHV badge has expired?
bank.explanation: Operating a vehicle as a PHV without a valid, current badge is a serious offence that can lead to prosecution and a future ban from the trade
options: You will receive a verbal warning from the operator
You will be fined GBP 10 but can continue working
Nothing, as long as you have applied for the renewal
You are driving without valid insurance and can be prosecuted

bank.question: When must a driver notify the Licensing Authority about a new medical condition that may affect their driving?
bank.explanation: A driver must notify the Licensing Authority in writing of any change to their medical status that may affect their ability to drive
options: Only when the driver's badge is up for renewal
As soon as the medical condition is diagnosed
Only if the driver is hospitalised for more than a week
Within 28 days of the condition improving

bank.question: Failing to display your external licence plates in the manner prescribed by the council is a breach of licensing conditions
bank.explanation: The external plates are a key safety feature that allow the public and police to identify the vehicle as a licensed and insured private hire car

bank.question: Where is a Private Hire vehicle permitted to wait to pick up passengers who have not pre-booked?
bank.explanation: All private hire vehicles must be pre-booked through a licensed operator; they cannot be hailed or wait at ranks like Hackney Carriages
options: At a designated taxi rank
Outside a night club at closing time
In a bus lane during restricted hours
Private hire vehicles cannot wait at ranks or be hailed in the street

bank.question: If you move house, what is your legal obligation regarding your PHV driver's license?
bank.explanation: You must notify the licensing authority in writing within a specific timeframe (usually 7 days) of any change to your home address
options: No action is needed as long as your operator knows your address
You only need to tell them when you renew your badge
You must notify the licensing authority in writing within 7 days
You only need to notify the DVLA, not the local council

bank.question: Who is legally responsible for ensuring a 7-year-old child uses an appropriate seatbelt or restraint in a Private Hire vehicle?
bank.explanation: The driver is responsible for ensuring children under 14 use the seat belts provided or the correct child restraint
options: The driver
The child's parent or guardian
The Private Hire Operator
The child themselves

bank.question: It is at the driver's discretion whether or not to charge an extra fee for carrying a registered assistance dog
bank.explanation: Unless you have a specific medical exemption certificate issued by the council, you are legally required to carry assistance dogs free of charge

bank.question: What is a major insurance risk if a Private Hire driver picks up a passenger who has not pre-booked through an operator?
bank.explanation: Plying for hire (picking up unbooked passengers) usually invalidates your hire and reward insurance, meaning you are effectively uninsured
options: The driver's licence will be instantly upgraded
The driver will receive a bonus from the operator
The vehicle's insurance policy may be invalidated
There are no consequences as long as the passenger pays

bank.question: Does holding a PHV driver badge allow you to pick up passengers in your own personal, unlicensed car?
bank.explanation: A PHV badge only permits you to carry passengers in a vehicle that is also licensed for private hire by the same authority
options: No, the vehicle must also be licensed for private hire
Yes, as long as you are wearing your badge
Yes, but only for trips shorter than 5 miles
Yes, if your personal insurance covers 'business use'

bank.question: Is a driver allowed to use an electronic cigarette (vape) inside their licensed Private Hire vehicle?
bank.explanation: Vaping is treated the same as smoking in licensed vehicles; it is prohibited at all times by most licensing authorities and smoke-free legislation
options: Yes, as long as a window is open
No, it is prohibited in licensed vehicles at all times
Yes, but only if there are no passengers in the car
Only if the passenger gives their verbal consent

bank.question: Accepting a passenger who approaches you on the street can invalidate your motor insurance policy
bank.explanation: Plying for hire (picking up unbooked passengers) can invalidate your hire and reward insurance, potentially leaving you and the passenger uncovered

bank.question: Regarding passenger luggage and assistance, what is the general expectation of a Private Hire driver?
bank.explanation: It is the driver's duty to provide reasonable assistance, such as helping with luggage or assisting a passenger into the vehicle
options: The driver is expected to offer reasonable assistance to passengers
The driver must stay in the car at all times for security reasons
The driver can charge an extra GBP 5 for any heavy lifting
The driver is only required to assist if the passenger is over 65

bank.question: Where is the legally required place to display your PHV driver badge while are on duty?
bank.explanation: By law, you must wear your badge in a position where it is clearly visible to passengers at all times while working
options: In your wallet or glove box for safekeeping
Hanging from the rear-view mirror
Pinned to your clothing or on a lanyard where it is clearly visible
In the boot of the car with your first aid kit

bank.question: What must a driver do with their badge if their Private Hire licence is suspended or revoked?
bank.explanation: The PHV driver's badge is the property of the Licensing Authority and must be returned if the licence is suspended, revoked, or expires
options: Throw it away or recycle it
Keep it at home as a souvenir
Give it to a friend who is also a driver
Return it to the Licensing Authority immediately

bank.question: Under what circumstances can a PHV badge holder legally accept a fare shouted from the street?
bank.explanation: A PHV badge holder may only accept bookings that have been pre-cleared and dispatched by a licensed operator
options: If the passenger is a regular customer of yours
If the passenger is standing directly outside your
If the passenger offers to pay double the usual fare
Under no circumstances; all bookings must go through a licensed operator

bank.question: If a licensed driver changes their home address, what action must they take?
bank.explanation: If a driver changes their residential address, they must inform the licensing department in writing within the specific timeframe (usually 7 days) as per the licensing conditions
options: Wait until the licence is up for renewal
Notify the Licensing Authority in writing within 7 days
They only need to tell their operator
No notification is required if they stay in the same city

bank.question: What is the likely penalty for a PHV badge holder found 'plying for hire' in the street?
bank.explanation: Plying for hire (picking up unbooked street hails) is a serious offence and typically leads to immediate badge revocation and prosecution
options: A small fine and a verbal warning from the operator
Immediate revocation of your badge and potential prosecution
A temporary 24-hour suspension of your license
Nothing, as long as you report the fare to your operator later

bank.question: When is a Private Hire vehicle permitted to drive in a bus lane?
bank.explanation: Private Hire vehicles are not permitted to use bus lanes unless specific local signage explicitly states that PHVs are allowed; otherwise, they are for buses, cyclists, and taxis (Hackney Carriages) only
options: Always, as they are part of the public transport network
Only when they have a passenger in the car
Only if they are responding to an emergency call
Only where the signs specifically include 'PHV' or 'Private Hire'

bank.question: Regarding passenger safety, what is a key responsibility of a PHV driver?
bank.explanation: PHV drivers have a duty of care to ensure all passengers, especially children, are seated safely according to the law
options: Ensuring the safety of all passengers and that children use correct restraints
Charging children a higher fare because they are more difficult to transport
Refusing to take any passenger under the age of 12 years old
Allowing children to sit in the footwell if the car is full

bank.question: What must a driver do with their badge once their Private Hire licence expires and is not renewed?
bank.explanation: The driver's badge remains the property of the Licensing Authority and must be returned immediately if the licence expires or is no longer in use
options: Keep it as a souvenir
Destroy it at home
Return it to the Licensing Authority immediately
Give it to their operator for safekeeping

bank.question: What should you do if your PHV driver badge is lost or stolen?
bank.explanation: You must report the loss to both the police (to get a reference number) and the licensing authority immediately to arrange a replacement
options: Continue working and tell the council when you next see them
Report it to the police and the licensing authority immediately
Make a temporary badge out of cardboard until a new one arrives
Borrow a badge from a friend who is not working that day

bank.question: A person flags you down in the street. How should you respond legally?
bank.explanation: Private Hire drivers must be pre-booked through a licensed operator. Picking up 'street hails' is known as 'plying for hire' and is illegal for PHV drivers
options: Politely refuse and explain they can only take pre-booked journeys through an operator
Agree to take them but charge double the usual rate
Take them as long as the journey is less than two miles
Let them in and then call the operator to 'back-book' the trip

bank.question: Who is authorised to ask to see your PHV driver badge for inspection at any reasonable time?
bank.explanation: Local authorities have the power to inspect badges at any time to ensure the driver is properly licensed and insured
options: Only a Police Officer in uniform
Only an official from the DVLA
A Police Officer or an authorised Licensing Officer
Your private hire operator's manager only

bank.question: What are a driver's duties regarding a passenger who uses a wheelchair?
bank.explanation: Drivers have a legal duty to provide reasonable physical assistance to passengers in wheelchairs without charging extra for the service
options: Refuse the booking if it takes too long to load the wheelchair
Charge a 'loading fee' for the extra time taken
Provide reasonable assistance to help the passenger enter and exit the vehicle
Ask the passenger to bring a friend to help them into the car

bank.question: Can a PHV driver badge holder refuse a booking because they do not like the destination?
bank.explanation: A PHV driver cannot refuse a pre-booked passenger based on their destination, even if it is a short trip or outside their usual area
options: No, you cannot refuse a booking without a reasonable excuse once accepted
Yes, if the journey is less than two miles long
Yes, but only if the passenger looks like they might not tip
Yes, if the destination is in an area you do not like driving in

bank.question: Where should the internal licence plate or disc be displayed in a Private Hire vehicle?
bank.explanation: Local licensing rules generally state that the 'Internal' licence plate or disc must be clearly visible to passengers inside the vehicle, often on the windscreen
options: In the glove box with the insurance documents
On the windscreen or dashboard where it is visible to passengers
Under the driver's seat for protection
On the rear parcel shelf facing backwards

bank.question: What are the general rules regarding a PHV badge holder's appearance and dress code?
bank.explanation: PHV drivers must maintain a high standard of personal hygiene and wear clean, professional clothing as per licensing conditions
options: There are no rules; you can wear whatever you like
You must wear a full three-piece suit at all times
You must be clean and tidy in your appearance and clothing
You must wear a high-visibility vest over your clothes

bank.question: What must a driver do if they receive a driving conviction or fixed penalty notice?
bank.explanation: All convictions, including driving offences and certain fixed penalties, must be reported to the Licensing Authority within the timeframe set in the policy
options: Only if it results in a driving ban
Only if it involves a passenger in the car
Wait until the annual background check (DBS) is performed
Notify the Licensing Authority in writing within the timeframe specified in their policy

bank.question: Which of the following describes the correct professional conduct for a licensed driver?
bank.explanation: PHV drivers are expected to be polite and helpful to all members of the public to maintain the reputation of the trade
options: Being silent and avoiding any eye contact with the passenger
Being polite and helpful to passengers and other road users
Driving as fast as possible to complete more bookings per hour
Demanding a tip before allowing the passenger to exit the vehicle

bank.question: Under what circumstances is a driver permitted to smoke inside a licensed Private Hire vehicle?
bank.explanation: The Health Act 2006 makes it illegal to smoke in a public transport vehicle at any time, even if no passengers are present
options: Never; it is illegal to smoke in a licensed vehicle at any time
Only when there are no passengers in the vehicle
Only if the driver has the window fully open
Only if the operator gives them permission

bank.question: What is the standard maximum duration for which a PHV driver badge is typically issued before it must be renewed?
bank.explanation: PHV driver badges are usually issued for a maximum of 3 years, though some authorities may issue 1-year licenses
options: Typically 3 years
Usually 10 years, same as a standard driving license
The badge never expires as long as you keep driving
Exactly 6 months from the date of issue

bank.question: Which of the following best describes the dress code requirements for a licensed Private Hire driver?
bank.explanation: Drivers must maintain high standards of personal hygiene and dress in a way that provides a professional image and does not cause offence
options: Any clothing they find comfortable, including swimwear
A full three-piece suit is mandatory for all shifts
A standard of dress that is clean, tidy, and professional
Whatever the passenger requests them to wear
